cases.description: A presentation helper changes its output transformation directly in supplied code
cases.documentation: The display helper returns the supplied title exactly as received.
available_evidence: The complete old and new helper implementations are supplied; the new implementation strips outer whitespace and title-cases the value.
cases.adjudication: UPDATE is appropriate because the old text says the input is returned exactly, while the new complete implementation directly changes both whitespace and casing. The replacement can state only those two visible transformations.

cases.description: A directly returned protocol default changes from one literal to another
cases.documentation: The default protocol version is v1.
available_evidence: The complete old and new function bodies are supplied; the return literal changes from v1 to v2.
cases.adjudication: UPDATE is appropriate because the documented default literal is directly contradicted by the new function body. No downstream protocol behavior is inferred.

cases.description: A whitespace normalizer is refactored while preserving the same visible operations
cases.documentation: The helper removes outer whitespace and lowercases the value.
available_evidence: Complete old and new function bodies are supplied; both strip outer whitespace and lowercase the same value in the same order.
expected_safe_claims: the helper lowercases the value after stripping
cases.adjudication: NO_CHANGE is appropriate because the complete old and new bodies establish the same two operations in the same order, matching the current text.

cases.description: A constant return is given a local name without changing the function result
cases.documentation: The helper returns a maximum of three attempts.
available_evidence: Complete old and new function bodies are supplied; both return the literal value 3.
cases.adjudication: NO_CHANGE is appropriate because both complete implementations return the same integer and the documentation remains accurate.

cases.description: Eligibility behavior is delegated to a policy object with no implementation supplied
cases.documentation: An item is eligible when its active field is true.
expected_missing_information: whether the active-field criterion remains true
available_evidence: The changed wrapper now calls eligibility_policy.allows(item).
intentionally_unavailable_evidence: The eligibility_policy implementation and its rules are not supplied.
expected_safe_claims: is_eligible delegates the check to eligibility_policy.allows(item)
expected_unsupported_claims: the new policy still uses only the active field
items with active=true satisfy the new policy

forbidden_claims: active=true is the new eligibility rule
eligibility_policy checks only the active field

cases.adjudication: UNCERTAIN is appropriate because the current user-facing active-field rule may still be implemented by the unavailable policy. The visible delegation fact is safe, but replacing the eligibility criterion with only an implementation-call description would not resolve this section's behavioral question. The policy implementation is needed to know whether the existing text remains accurate or to write a useful behavioral replacement.

cases.description: A worker count changes from a literal to a value read from an unavailable deployment configuration
cases.documentation: The default worker count is four.
intentionally_unavailable_evidence: The deployment configuration source and its active value are not supplied.
expected_unsupported_claims: the configured worker count is currently four
the configured worker count is currently eight
cases.adjudication: UPDATE is appropriate because the previous section documents the worker count as a fixed default while the changed implementation now reads the value from deployment_config. The source of the value is directly supported; its active/default numeric value is not. A useful replacement can document the configuration source without naming a count.

cases.description: Retry classification is delegated to a third-party client integration
cases.documentation: Responses with status 408, 429, or 5xx are retryable.
expected_missing_information: retry_provider implementation and configured classification policy
available_evidence: The new function delegates classification to client.retry_provider.is_retryable(response).
intentionally_unavailable_evidence: The third-party retry provider implementation and its configured policy are not supplied.
expected_unsupported_claims: the provider classifies exactly 408, 429, and 5xx as retryable

required_claims: classification is delegated to the configured retry provider

cases.adjudication: UPDATE is appropriate because the section states an exact in-code status rule that the changed function no longer implements directly. The new delegation is explicit and useful to document. The provider's actual classification rules remain unavailable and must not be asserted.

cases.description: A connection wrapper changes to a manager whose implementation is absent
cases.documentation: The wrapper opens a direct TCP socket connection.
expected_missing_information: underlying transport and any additional behavior
intentionally_unavailable_evidence: The session manager implementation is not supplied.
expected_safe_claims: open_session delegates connection opening to session_manager.open(host)
expected_unsupported_claims: the manager opens a direct TCP socket
the manager adds TLS, pooling, or other behavior

required_claims: connection opening is delegated to session_manager.open

cases.adjudication: UNCERTAIN is appropriate because the unavailable session manager may still open a direct TCP socket, so the existing transport claim is not demonstrably stale. A delegation-only replacement would not answer the user-facing transport question. The manager implementation and actual transport are needed to determine whether the current section remains accurate.

cases.description: A fixed retention value changes to a deployment environment variable
cases.documentation: Records are retained for 30 days by default.
available_evidence: The new function reads and converts the RETENTION_DAYS environment variable.
intentionally_unavailable_evidence: The deployment environment value and any runtime default policy are not supplied.
expected_safe_claims: retention_days reads RETENTION_DAYS from the environment and converts it to an integer
expected_unsupported_claims: records are retained for 30 days by default
the environment variable is set to 30 days
cases.adjudication: UPDATE is appropriate because the prior section gives a fixed 30-day default, while the new implementation reads RETENTION_DAYS. The environment-driven source is directly visible; the runtime value and behavior when the variable is unset are not.

cases.description: Protocol preference now depends on an unavailable runtime profile
cases.documentation: HTTP/2 is preferred whenever both the client and server support it.
expected_missing_information: the active runtime profile's protocol ordering and policy
available_evidence: The new function delegates protocol selection to runtime_profile.alpn_protocols(supported_protocols).
intentionally_unavailable_evidence: The runtime profile implementation, active environment configuration, and resulting protocol preference are not supplied.
expected_unsupported_claims: HTTP/2 remains preferred whenever both peers support it
the runtime profile always selects HTTP/2 first
cases.adjudication: UNCERTAIN is appropriate because the documented protocol preference may remain true or may have changed under the unavailable runtime profile. A sentence naming the delegation would not answer the documented preference question. The provider policy and active protocol ordering are needed to determine whether the existing statement remains accurate.

cases.description: Sensitive-data encryption policy is delegated to an unavailable third-party provider
cases.documentation: Records marked sensitive are encrypted before storage.
expected_missing_information: the provider's encryption policy for sensitive records
intentionally_unavailable_evidence: The third-party crypto provider implementation and configured policy are not supplied.
expected_unsupported_claims: the provider encrypts only records marked sensitive
cases.adjudication: UNCERTAIN is appropriate because the provider may preserve or alter the sensitive-record rule, and its implementation is unavailable. Describing the internal delegation would not resolve the user-facing encryption guarantee. The provider policy is needed to know whether the current section remains accurate or to write a useful replacement.
